steps.message:
Curve-type notation for vertical electrical sounding (VES): take the layer resistivities in depth order. For each group of three consecutive layers (layers 1-2-3, then 2-3-4, and so on), write one letter: A if r1 < r2 < r3; Q if r1 > r2 > r3; H if r1 > r2 < r3; K if r1 < r2 > r3. A curve with N layers gets N-2 letters, in depth order (for example, a 4-layer curve gets 2 letters, such as HA). If all the letters are the same, the curve may also be written as that single letter (AAA may be written A).

Station Ndashi, Etche LGA survey stations. Interpreted layer model:

Layer | Resistivity (ohm-m) | Thickness (m) | Depth to base (m)
----- | ------------------- | ------------- | -----------------
1 | 13.515 | 0.49701 | 0.49701
2 | 1257.2 | 1.5896 | 2.0866
3 | 2041.3 | 4.5367 | 6.6232
4 | 1765.4 | 17.594 | 24.217
5 | 77.636 | 16.33 | 30.85
6 | 2384.1 | - | -

What is the curve type of this station? Give a short answer, then end with one JSON line exactly like this:
{"curve_type": "<letters>"}

To determine the curve-type notation for the given vertical electrical sounding (VES) data, we examine the resistivity of each consecutive group of three layers.

The resistivities are:
1. $r_1 = 13.515$
2. $r_2 = 1257.2$
3. $r_3 = 2041.3$
4. $r_4 = 1765.4$
5. $r_5 = 77.636$
6. $r_6 = 2384.1$

Now, we evaluate each group of three:
- **Layers 1-2-3:** $13.515 < 1257.2 < 2041.3$ ($r_1 < r_2 < r_3$). This corresponds to **A**.
- **Layers 2-3-4:** $1257.2 < 2041.3 > 1765.4$ ($r_2 < r_3 > r_4$). This corresponds to **K**.
- **Layers 3-4-5:** $2041.3 > 1765.4 > 77.636$ ($r_3 > r_4 > r_5$). This corresponds to **Q**.
- **Layers 4-5-6:** $1765.4 > 77.636 < 2384.1$ ($r_4 > r_5 < r_6$). This corresponds to **H**.

Combining these letters in depth order gives the sequence AKQH.

{"curve_type": "AKQH"}
